content.body:
The heavier Allied tanks met on the battlefield, such as the Matilda II, forced the German High Command to reconsider all of their AFV armaments, so the StuG III B was up-gunned to the longer 75 mm simultaneously with the Panzer IV series upgrades.
Improving some of the more egregious design failings of the B, this resulted in the StuG III G, a very effective tank destroyer produced far more cheaply and quickly than its more complicated, turreted cousins. Nearly 10,000 were ultimately produced and deployed into every theater of the war. As the tide of the conflict for the Germans turned from offensive to defensive, the ambush AFVs like the StuG III G became more and more useful and preferred in production. Like the Panzer IV G, the more lethal anti-tank ability of the 75 mm meant that HEAT ammunition was no longer included as standard ammo.
The utility of the StuG III G depends a great deal on the tactical situation. If on the defensive, the StuG III G is probably the best ambusher of the game. Its low profile, camouflage, and fire power mean that it will usually win if it gets the first shot. On the offensive, it is harder to use. If spotted, Allied opponents will hunt you down with great dedication. Without a turret it is often hard to get into a good firing position without completely exposing your tank.
As expected for a turret-less tank, situational awareness ("SA") is a problem and the limited ammo stocks remain a serious limit on the StuG's ability to sustain a gun duel or hold a position in the face of a persistent attack. On the plus side, even if you are identified, the heavy front armor means good protection for withdrawal.
Lacking a defensive machinegune, the StuG is at the mercy of close-in enemy infantry. If you identify infantry around you, just pack up and run; if they are sappers then they may already be planting a charge on you and even if they are just regular infantry they will use smoke grenades to mark you as a target or prevent you firing when the sappers show up. And sappers will show up because StuGs are hated by all those who must fight them. So do not stick around!
Note: HE rounds tend to fall shorter than AP rounds, especially at long ranges. Unlike the Panzer IV G, the StuG III G does not have the two-tier range setting system in the gun sight. If you are going to be using a StuG III G a lot, it is worthwhile to jump into a Panzer IV G offline and jot down some corresponding ranges for reference when shooting the StuG III G 75 mm gun.
Control Variations: Crew 1 driver has a non-zoom view slit to his left. Crew 2 Commander may use the numpad 0 or Ins key to look through periscopes of his cupola without exposing himself outside the tank. He may not use his included rangefinder unless he unbuttons, however. Crew 3 must still deploy a sight to aim the gun, but in this case it peeks out of a small roof hole instead of opening the shot-trap view slit.
